attrs.evidence: Fable proposed promoting the ledger's `hypothesis`/`assumptions` fields wholesale into a Contract Registry; GPT-5.6 refused the collapse, correctly — a theorem's antecedent and a component's interface contract are not one semantic object even when they share a predicate. One vocabulary, seven kinds, and contracts reference records rather than duplicating them: that keeps Fable's instinct (do not write the same rule twice) without pretending the three contexts mean the same thing. THE CONCRETE REASON: TAX-RELATIONAL-2's prose assumption cites `NEW-27A-OBSERVER`, an id no record in this ledger has ever carried — the record is TAX-27A-OBSERVER. Prose can name a record that does not exist and nothing refuses it; an id can be checked, and now is.
attrs.gap: 18 assumption records exist and 19 claims reference them. The other 45 claims still carry prose-only assumptions, and CONDITIONAL is the only status where the gate demands ids.
attrs.prior_art: Benveniste et al., contract meta-theory (assume-guarantee); the theorem/contract split is GPT-5.6's correction of Fable's merge.
attrs.statement: Assumptions are one vocabulary with a kind discriminator — theorem, environment, interface, observer, distribution, substrate, resource — and a claim references assumption records by id rather than restating them in prose.
